newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia maintains tight grip on inflation.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia maintains tight grip on inflation.

text.p: Indonesia reported strong economic data on Wednesday, with monthly inflation falling in September and its trade surplus widening.
Indonesia's consumer price index (CPI) declined 0.04 percent month-on-month in September, against a rise of 0.27 percent in August, Information Minister Harmoko said.
The country posted a trade surplus of $508.5 million in July, compared with $193.4 million in June, he told reporters after the monthly cabinet meeting.
"Our inflation in September is at a good level. I think we can control our inflation to around seven percent in 1996," Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita told Reuters.
"We will continue to manage our economy very carefully despite the decline in September," Ginanjar said.

Harmoko said September's decline in consumer prices reflected a drop in food prices, while prices for housing, textiles and services rose. Food prices declined 0.76 percent in September against a drop of 0.35 percent in August.
Year-on-year inflation in September was 6.79 percent against 7.21 percent in August.

Harmoko said President Suharto had asked the logistics bureau (Bulog) to prepare market operations and supply rice, vegetable oil and sugar to meet anticipated higher overall demand for food in the last quarter of the year.
Bulog buys essential commodities from producers and supplies them to the market at controlled prices.
"Bulog is ordered to prepare market operations to stabilise prices," Harmoko said.

"The inflation is following a trend which we have seen in the past few months. It is going down gradually. That is in line with market expectations," Sani Hamid, an emerging market analyst with MMS International in Singapore, told Reuters.
"The trend should continue. People are starting to revise CPI downward to around 7.1 or 7.2 percent for 1996," he said.
However, the Central Bureau of Statistics said in a report last month that annual inflation was forecast to reach 8.5 percent in 1996 and 8.9 percent in 1997.
Indonesia's annual inflation in 1995 was 8.64 percent.
The bureau said higher inflation was expected to reflect stronger demand rather than slower growth on the supply side.
The government has targeted an average annual inflation rate of five percent in the current five-year development period, ending in 1999. It has yet to be achieved.
Harmoko said Suharto had also ordered Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo to simplify export rules to boost the country's exports.

He said total exports rose to $4.06 billion in July from $4.13 billion in June. Oil and gas exports edged up to $909.7 million in July from $828.4 in June. Imports fell to $3.58 billion in July from $3.94 billion in June.
